Seed molecule (SMILES): C#Cc1cccc(Nc2ncnc3cc(OCCOC)c(OCCOC)cc23)c1
Optimisation objectives stated by the user: User explicitly asks to propose structural analogues of a named molecule (erlotinib) and provide their SMILES, which is a generate_analogs task; no target or optimization objective was specified.
Propose 10 distinct single-point edits.

request.system: You are a medicinal chemist proposing structural edits. Return complete, valid SMILES for each edited molecule -- not fragments, not reaction arrows, not names. Keep the core recognisable: single-point modifications such as substituent changes, bioisosteric replacements, ring swaps or linker adjustments. Never claim an activity value; the edits will be scored by independent tools.

tools.name: propose_edits
tools.description: Propose medicinal-chemistry edits of a seed molecule as SMILES.

smiles.description: Full SMILES of the edited molecule.

edits.rationale: Extended one methoxyethoxy chain to methoxypropoxy-like ethyl homolog to probe effect of side-chain length on the quinazoline 6-position
Replaced one terminal methyl ether with a free hydroxyl to increase polarity and H-bond donor count
Swapped one methoxyethoxy substituent for a dimethylaminoethoxy group to introduce a basic amine and modulate solubility
Added a fluorine on the aniline ring (ortho to the alkyne) as a bioisosteric halogen substitution to tune electronics and metabolic stability
Inserted a methylene spacer between the aryl ring and alkyne (propargyl instead of direct ethynyl) to modulate rigidity and electronic conjugation
Replaced the terminal alkyne with a methyl group to remove the reactive/electrophilic alkyne while retaining similar sterics
Replaced one methoxyethoxy chain with a trifluoroethoxy-ethoxy group to increase lipophilicity and metabolic stability via fluorination
Substituted one methoxyethoxy arm with a cyclopropylmethoxy group as a bioisosteric replacement to reduce flexibility
Replaced the aniline benzene ring with a pyridine (aza-substitution) to modulate electronics and add a hydrogen-bond acceptor
Added a chlorine substituent ortho to the alkyne on the aniline ring to explore steric and electronic effects of halogenation
